driver_review: Unittest suite is loaded from the pinned new test file, run failfast, persisted, and required to succeed without skipped tests before benchmark starts.

The unmocked benchmark selects original_score, prior.score_forecast, or candidate.score_forecast by the explicit original/poisson/skellam mode. Candidate scorer constructs SkellamDistribution, whose _cdf calls the new helper in exactly the correlated and independent margin branches.

The candidate helper uses the pinned SciPy private backend with length-one int64/float64 arrays, clipping and scalar extraction; unsupported arguments delegate unchanged to the generic public function. Actual passing focused tests exercise backend argument identity, dispatch and error outcomes.

Each benchmark observation invokes real _Assembly.resolve and separately times complete score_forecast with double_grid=True and diagnostics=True; one fit and one recovery are asserted. No cProfile or helper-only timer is used.
The original encoder is retained for every mode; no patch is applied by the benchmark. saved.encoded identity is asserted after every observation and at completion.
Complete descriptor/metric bodies are saved before equality checks against pinned earlier original references. All observations, including every warmup and rotated round, are present.

The retained source map and source snapshots authenticate the candidate, tests, driver, SciPy implementation/backend binary, prior accepted evidence and 66 original sources. No scientific module was imported or executed by this review.
limitations: This reviewer authored the focused tests; this is not independent numerical acceptance. Separate numerical and timing review remains required.
Passing finite synthetic cases do not prove equality on every admissible input or historical feasibility. Backend behavior is pinned to the recorded runtime and library source/binary hashes.

Canonical recovered-law hashes are retained and compared; raw law arrays and benchmark grids are not persisted for independent rehash here. The passing focused suite separately compares actual primary/doubled grid arrays and bounds.

Runtime/branch invocation evidence comes from the authenticated source, assertions and retained outputs, not an external instruction trace. No new profiling or callback invocation occurred during review.

The recorded process clock begins after importing time; interpreter startup and the final process-report write tail are excluded. Parent child-RSS sampling/wait accounting is not a historical runtime guarantee.

The benchmark deliberately uses a tiny genuine synthetic bank and bypasses archive admission/complete assembly construction. Unit/fixture computations are included in process resources but excluded from its 168+168 callback counters.
No historical admission, new historical score, bootstrap, model acceptance, restart or production authorization follows from this result.
